hints: Notice the diagram shows field lines that are parallel and evenly spaced around P, with Y along the lines and X across them.
Recall that parallel evenly spaced lines represent a uniform field where electric field strength $E$ has the same magnitude and direction at every point.
Use $F = qE$ for the fixed positive charge $q$ on P to compare the force before and after a small move in Y, Z or X.
walkthrough: Identify the field pattern: the lines of force near P are stated to be evenly spaced and parallel and drawn as straight vertical arrows.
State the physical rule: evenly spaced parallel field lines mean a uniform electric field, so $E$ is constant in both magnitude and direction.
Apply the force rule for a charged particle: $F = qE$, where $q$ is the constant positive charge of P.
Argue the cause and effect: because $q$ and $E$ are both unchanged by a small displacement in direction X, Y, Z or any other direction, $F$ is also unchanged.
Conclude that moving P a small distance in any direction will not change the electric force on P. This is option A.

options.A: The field is uniform so $E$ is the same everywhere and $F = qE$ on P does not change with a small displacement.
options.B: Direction Y is along the field lines, but in a uniform field moving along the lines does not change $E$ or $F$.
options.C: Direction Z is opposite to the field lines, but field strength does not increase toward the bottom in an evenly spaced parallel pattern.
options.D: Direction X is across the field lines, but the even spacing shows $E$ is constant so moving sideways does not increase $F$.
